install.note: OpenScience is an open-source, model-agnostic AI research desktop workbench. The desktop app bundles the OpenScience runtime. Its current in-app updater is macOS-only; Windows and Linux users should install newer releases from the official download page. Windows supports x64; macOS supports Apple Silicon and Intel; Linux ships x64 and arm64 AppImages. Stable macOS DMGs are signed and notarized. The Windows installer and Linux AppImages are currently unsigned, so explain the expected operating-system warning before opening them. EchoBird configures the model through OpenScience's resolved config directory (`OPENSCIENCE_CONFIG_DIR`, then `XDG_CONFIG_HOME/openscience`, then `~/.config/openscience`) and marks the local desktop onboarding complete in `settings.json`, so an EchoBird-configured third-party model does not require a Synthetic Sciences account. The desktop app must be fully restarted after an external model change. The CLI remains a separate upstream option, but desktop-app requests must use these desktop installers rather than npm, `npx synsci`, the shell installer, or CLI archives.

install_flow.summary: Detect OS and architecture, download the matching official desktop installer, open it for the user, then let EchoBird configure a third-party model and complete local onboarding.
agent_steps: Install only on the local machine with a graphical desktop. Detect OS and CPU architecture first. Windows supports x64 only; macOS supports arm64 and x64; Linux supports arm64 and x64. If the platform or architecture is unsupported, point the user to https://www.openscience.sh/download and do not substitute a CLI build.

Download the matching URL from install to the user's Downloads folder using a resolved full path: OpenScienceSetup.exe on Windows, OpenScience.dmg on macOS, or OpenScience.AppImage on Linux. If a latest-download URL fails, read https://www.openscience.sh/download or the official GitHub Releases page for the current desktop asset; do not use a lowercase `openscience-*` CLI archive as a desktop installer.

Before opening Windows or Linux builds, tell the user that the official build is currently unsigned and the OS may show a security warning. Do not disable SmartScreen, Gatekeeper, antivirus, or other operating-system protections.

Windows: open the downloaded NSIS installer with `Start-Process -FilePath <resolved-path>` without `-Wait`. Tell the user to choose the install directory and finish the wizard; do not invent or use silent flags. Stop the turn after handing off the installer.

macOS: open the downloaded DMG with `open <resolved-path>`, tell the user to drag OpenScience.app to Applications, then stop the turn. The stable DMG is signed and notarized; do not use the ZIP updater payload as the installer.

Linux: create `~/.local/bin` if needed, move the downloaded file to `~/.local/bin/OpenScience.AppImage`, mark it executable, and launch it detached. Tell the user exactly where it was saved and that desktop-menu integration may depend on their desktop environment; then stop the turn.

When the user returns after the installer or first launch is complete, verify OpenScience through the installed application path or OS application registration. Do not verify the desktop install with `openscience --version`, because that tests the separate CLI.

Have the user select and apply a third-party model for OpenScience in EchoBird. That operation writes the `echobird` provider and active-model selectors to `openscience.json` in OpenScience's resolved config directory, preserves unrelated settings, and sets `desktop_onboarding_version` to the supported local completion revision with `desktop_onboarding_step` set to `done` in the sibling `settings.json`. This skips only the local setup gate; it does not fabricate a Synthetic Sciences session or unlock account-only managed services.

Use Apply & Launch after model configuration. EchoBird fully restarts the desktop app so it reloads the new local configuration. Provider sign-in and credentials not managed by EchoBird remain the user's actions inside OpenScience.
tell_user: Detected OS and architecture and the matching desktop asset
The exact saved installer or AppImage path
That Windows and Linux desktop builds are currently unsigned and may trigger an OS warning
Whether the installer or app was opened and which user steps remain
That applying an EchoBird model completes local onboarding without creating a Synthetic Sciences login
After the user finishes, whether the installed desktop app was verified and launched
